title: Use EXISTS instead of a fan-out join in asset orphanage
body:
`SchedulerJobRunner._update_asset_orphanage` outer-joins `asset` to four independent one-to-many tables (`dag_schedule_asset_reference`, `task_outlet_asset_reference`, `task_inlet_asset_reference`, `asset_alias_asset`) and groups by `asset.id`. The joins multiply: each asset produces `schedule_refs * outlet_refs * inlet_refs * aliases` rows before the `GROUP BY`. The result is used in three statements (orphan `DELETE`, active `SELECT`, inactive `SELECT`).

A handful of popular assets (many consumers, many producing tasks) is enough to push this past Postgres `statement_timeout`. On one of our deployments (~11.7k assets, 4 scheduler replicas) the activation query hit the timeout on every orphanage pass, about every 20s. Since the timer is not `non_fatal`, that stalled the scheduler loop and caused intermittent 503s. It got noticeably worse on 3.3, when the alias association join (#58058) added a fourth factor.

This replaces the join and `GROUP BY` with one `EXISTS` per reference table. Each is served by an index led by `asset_id` (the three reference tables' primary keys and `idx_asset_alias_asset_asset_id`), stops at the first match, and doesn't multiply rows. The CTEs keep the same columns, so `_orphan_unreferenced_assets` and `_activate_referenced_assets` are unchanged.

Tests: existing orphanage tests pass unchanged, plus a new case where one asset has several references in every table.

Would appreciate the `backport-to-v3-3-test` label if this looks right, since 3.3 is where the regression shows up.

@@ -4217,30 +4217,17 @@ def _update_asset_orphanage(self, *, session: Session = NEW_SESSION) -> None:
 
         :seealso: :meth:`AssetModelOperation.activate_assets_if_possible`.
         """
-        # Group assets into orphaned=True and orphaned=False groups.
-        orphaned = (
-            (
-                func.count(DagScheduleAssetReference.dag_id)
-                + func.count(TaskOutletAssetReference.dag_id)
-                + func.count(TaskInletAssetReference.dag_id)
-                # An asset materialized from an ``AssetAlias`` outlet is referenced only through
-                # the alias association, not the schedule/outlet/inlet tables. Count it so it is
-                # activated (and shown in the UI) instead of being treated as orphaned. See #58058.
-                + func.count(alias_association_table.c.alias_id)
-            )
-            == 0
-        ).label("orphaned")
-        asset_reference_query = (
-            select(AssetModel)
-            .outerjoin(DagScheduleAssetReference)
-            .outerjoin(TaskOutletAssetReference)
-            .outerjoin(TaskInletAssetReference)
-            .outerjoin(alias_association_table, alias_association_table.c.asset_id == AssetModel.id)
-            .group_by(AssetModel.id)
+        referenced = or_(
+            exists().where(DagScheduleAssetReference.asset_id == AssetModel.id),
+            exists().where(TaskOutletAssetReference.asset_id == AssetModel.id),
+            exists().where(TaskInletAssetReference.asset_id == AssetModel.id),
+            # An asset materialized from an ``AssetAlias`` outlet is referenced only through
+            # the alias association, not the schedule/outlet/inlet tables. Count it so it is
+            # activated (and shown in the UI) instead of being treated as orphaned. See #58058.
+            exists().where(alias_association_table.c.asset_id == AssetModel.id),
         )
-
-        orphan_query = asset_reference_query.having(orphaned).cte()
-        activate_query = asset_reference_query.having(~orphaned).cte()
+        orphan_query = select(AssetModel).where(~referenced).cte()
+        activate_query = select(AssetModel).where(referenced).cte()
 
         self._orphan_unreferenced_assets(orphan_query, session=session)
         self._activate_referenced_assets(activate_query, session=session)

+        self.job_runner = SchedulerJobRunner(job=Job())
+
+        shared = Asset(uri="test://shared", name="shared", group="test_group")
+        dropped = Asset(uri="test://dropped", name="dropped", group="test_group")
+
+        for i in range(3):
+            with dag_maker(dag_id=f"consumer-{i}", schedule=[shared], session=session):
+                BashOperator(task_id="task", bash_command="echo 1")
+        with dag_maker(dag_id="producer", schedule=None, session=session):
+            for i in range(3):
+                BashOperator(task_id=f"produce-{i}", bash_command="echo 1", outlets=[shared, dropped])
+                BashOperator(task_id=f"read-{i}", bash_command="echo 1", inlets=[shared])
+
+        self.job_runner._update_asset_orphanage(session=session)
+        session.flush()
+        orphaned, active = self._find_assets_activation(session)
+        assert active == [dropped, shared]

+

+                BashOperator(task_id=f"read-{i}", bash_command="echo 1", inlets=[shared])
+
+        self.job_runner._update_asset_orphanage(session=session)
